title: Advanced Compiler and Execution Techniques
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of advanced compiler and execution techniques in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of advanced compiler and execution techniques and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Advanced Compiler and Execution Techniques: Performance engineering begins with measurement. Profilers show which operators and stages consume time or memory; compilation and layout changes should be measured after warm-up. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: Optimizations can add compile overhead, complexity, or accuracy changes. A stable baseline helps distinguish real improvement from noise. For this lesson, focus on compilation backends and modes and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Profile a representative workload, identify a bottleneck, change one factor, warm up, synchronize accelerators when measuring, then compare latency, throughput, memory, and outputs. The source topics for this lesson are: Compilation backends and modes, Compile-time and runtime trade-offs, Shape-specialized execution. Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.title: Read the example
content_blocks.text: Read the profiler output as evidence about the measured sample, not a universal ranking. For compiled functions, separate first-call compilation cost from steady-state execution. The example is a teaching-scale check, not evidence of a trained model score or a hardware-independent performance claim.

items.title: Compilation backends and modes
items.text: Connect this topic to the lesson workflow: Profile a representative workload, identify a bottleneck, change one factor, warm up, synchronize accelerators when measuring, then compare latency, throughput, memory, and outputs. Write down the expected behavior and test it on a small, inspectable input.

items.title: Compile-time and runtime trade-offs
items.text: Measure a representative baseline with warm-up and repeated trials, change one factor, and re-check output quality before claiming improvement.

items.title: Shape-specialized execution
items.text: Write down the expected axes and element count, then assert the observed shape. For layout-related topics, also check contiguity and whether storage is shared.

items.title: Compiled training and inference
items.text: Measure a representative baseline with warm-up and repeated trials, change one factor, and re-check output quality before claiming improvement.

items.title: Benchmarking under realistic workloads
items.text: Record the artifact state and environment assumptions, restore it in a clean model, and verify behavior on a fixed input before trusting the result.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.code:
import torch
compiled = torch.compile(lambda x: x + 1)
print(torch.equal(compiled(torch.tensor([1])), torch.tensor([2])))
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as example.py in a Python environment with a compatible PyTorch installation, then run `python example.py`. PyTorch snippets are not executed in the browser. For GPU- or package-specific snippets, install the matching supported dependencies first.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the code block, rerun it, and compare both the printed output and tensor metadata.

content.task: Try it yourself: Profile a small tensor workload and record a baseline; make one simple change and explain whether the evidence supports an improvement. Record the observed result and one limitation; do not report an unrun training or performance result as measured.
task_acceptance_criteria: The experiment demonstrates at least one relevant aspect of advanced compiler and execution techniques.
Record the expected and observed result, including shape/dtype/device information when relevant.
Explain one common failure mode, compatibility limitation, or evaluation caveat.
hints: Begin with the smallest working example for advanced compiler and execution techniques and keep input shapes explicit.
Change only one variable at a time; compare a tensor property, a printed value, or a test assertion.
Use the linked official reference for any hardware-specific, optional-package, or version-sensitive behavior.

troubleshooting.symptom: A tensor operation raises a shape, dtype, or device mismatch.
troubleshooting.check: Print .shape, .dtype, and .device for each input. Resolve the mismatch intentionally instead of changing dimensions blindly.

troubleshooting.symptom: The example fails because an optional package or accelerator is unavailable.
troubleshooting.check: Check the installed PyTorch/package versions and device availability. Use the official installation selector and run the CPU-compatible path where appropriate.

troubleshooting.symptom: The result differs across runs or machines.
troubleshooting.check: Fix the seed where useful, record versions and inputs, and document operations that remain nondeterministic or hardware dependent.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not publish a performance claim from one unsynchronized timing sample or a different workload.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.
